summary: Reports President Ali's naming of a five-member Commission of Inquiry: Justice Godfrey Phillip Smith of Belize as chair, Dr Andrzej Jasionowski, Capt. Hamada Fouda, Nyree Dawn Alfonso and Rear Admiral (Ret'd) Hayden A. Pritchard. States Smith previously served on the COI into Guyana's 2 March 2020 elections, and quotes Ali that the legal instruments are “currently being formalised”. Gives 179 aboard, 76 rescued, 73 bodies recovered, at least 30 unaccounted for. Records Opposition Leader Azruddin Mohamed's, APNU's and Dr Terrence Campbell's objections to the absence of consultation.

Reports that two hinterland leaders are calling for Minister Juan Edghill's resignation. Kako Toshao Romario Hastings states that politics shaped appointments and resource prioritisation, that fear of political retribution silences other Toshaos, and that he would have resigned in the Minister's place. Chris Debideen, Chairman of the Aruau Community Development Council, states he lost two relatives, questions the elapsed time before rescuers responded, calls for modernised vessels, and argues a double standard between the removal of Indigenous leaders for mismanagement and the retention of ministers.

An opinion column published under Kaieteur News's “Peeping Tom” byline, carrying the paper's disclaimer, arguing against the Minister's resignation at this stage. It distinguishes collective from individual ministerial responsibility, argues the Transport & Harbours Department's own board insulates the Minister from day-to-day operations, and proposes Cabinet support, National Assembly acceptance and sustained non-partisan public loss of trust as tests. It states the cause is not yet established and cites the 2017 Camp Street prison fire, in which 18 died without a ministerial resignation.

Kiskadee Watch gives a chronology of the unfinished Port Kaituma stelling, which the Prime Minister cited as the reason the MV Ma Lisha could not serve the route. States the G$1.4bn construction contract was awarded by public tender to International Import and Supplies on 30 December 2022, with design and supervision by CEMCO. Reports work halted in February 2024 at about 90 per cent; the contractor stated the cause was design, not construction, and Minister Edghill stated CEMCO acknowledged design flaws. States no completion date has been given.

Reports that a 15-member specialist dive team from the French Armed Forces in French Guiana told relatives of the missing that entering the wreck is too dangerous, citing ropes and hammocks inside, mud, darkness and strong tidal currents. The unnamed diver states about 15 dives were completed between Tuesday and 27 July, and that lifting the vessel would be “very, very difficult”. Gives 179 aboard, 76 rescued, 73 bodies recovered, at least 30 unaccounted for.
